title: fix(plugin-view): assert the ViewType totals instead of annotating them exactly
body:
Fixes #9943

⚠️ **Type arguments are written in SQUARE brackets throughout this body** — `Record[ViewType, string]` means `Record` applied to `ViewType` and `string`. GitHub's body sanitizer deletes tag-shaped tokens, and a generic is one; fences and code spans do not protect them. The source carries the real angle-bracket spelling.

Three tables in `plugin-view` are total over the **whole** `ViewType` and carried the annotation `Record[ViewType, X]`. An annotated object literal is **exact in both directions**, and only one of those directions was ever wanted:

- it catches a member the spec **ADDS** — the guard objectui#5321 installed on `iconMap` and objectui#8127 installed on the switcher's pair;
- it also makes a member the spec **RETIRES** an excess property, TS2353, whose only repair is deleting the row.

objectstack#17063 retired the list-view kind `page`, so all three go red against a spec built from objectstack `main` — while the `@objectstack/spec` this repository **resolves** still publishes `page` and an author can still write one. The row cannot be deleted and the annotation cannot stay.

## The repair, and why it is ⛔ NOT objectui#9880's

objectui#9880's two tables **partition** the drawable half, so it repaired them by *deriving* the undrawable half with `Extract[ViewType, keyof typeof TABLE]`: a retired row drops out of the type on its own while staying live at runtime. **These three partition nothing** — they are total over the whole union — so there is no second half to derive from and that shape does not transfer.

What replaces the annotation is `satisfies Record[string, X]` (value constraint kept, exactness dropped) **plus a separate totality assert**, spelled in the source as a one-line helper `_AssertNever` whose parameter is constrained to `never`, applied to `Exclude[ViewType, keyof typeof TABLE]`. While every member has a row that `Exclude` is `never` and the alias compiles; the day a member has none it is a live union and the alias fails with TS2344.

⛔ The assert is not decoration. `satisfies Record[string, X]` **alone** would make `page` inert and silently stop catching an added member — trading one guard for the other. Both directions are pinned, with the failing spellings kept as firing controls.

## A fourth site, in a file this diff had to touch anyway

`ViewSwitcher.test.tsx`'s `ALL_VIEW_TYPES` carried `satisfies Record[ViewType, true]`. That is **not** the repair spelling and fails identically: `satisfies` runs the same excess-property check, measured on a simulated retired vocabulary — `TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'page' does not exist in type 'Record[ViewTypeMain, true]'`. It is repaired the same way. Same defect class, same package, mechanical, same gate family; the file was already in the diff because it carries a source-text anchor on `iconMap`'s declaration line.

## Two readers this diff would otherwise have broken

| reader | what broke | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` anchored-map extractor | it tested `ts.isObjectLiteralExpression(node.initializer)`, which is **FALSE** when a `SatisfiesExpression` wraps the literal. Two of its shipped anchors (`iconMap`, `DEFAULT_VIEW_ICONS`) are on that spelling now. | with the unwrap disabled the gate exits 1: ``anchored map `iconMap` … yielded 0 entries, fewer than the 9 it is known to carry``, **and the same for `DEFAULT_VIEW_ICONS`** |
| `ViewSwitcher.test.tsx`'s `parseMapEntries` | it ended a literal at the two characters `};`, which a `} satisfies …;` line does not contain | **latent, not live** — see the falsified prediction below |

The gate now unwraps `satisfies` / `as` / parentheses before reading, with its own suite extended to cover both wrappers plus a non-object initializer (the `min` precondition must still fire there).

## Verification

Final commit `4e356208a`, base `706e09f27`.

| leg | command | reading |
|---|---|---|
| type-check | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-view run type-check` | **exit 0** (two programs: `tsconfig.json` + `tsconfig.test.json`) |
| tests | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-view/ scripts/__tests__/check-lucide-icon-record-names.test.ts scripts/__tests__/lucide-record-icon-names-generated-9251.test.ts scripts/__tests__/unit-registry-absence-collision.test.ts` | **47 files, 469 tests, all passed** |
| lint | `pnpm exec eslint .` from the repo root, `--format json` | **5146 files judged, 0 errors, 13205 warnings** — the whole population, **no narrowing**. ⛔ No `--no-inline-config` added. |
| icon gate | `node scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` | `OK lucide icon names: 184 … are live icons keys` — **184 both before and after**, so the unwrap reads the same population it always did |
| governed | `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the final file list | `✅ NOT GOVERNED — 7 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.` |
| changeset | `check-changeset-presence` / `-fixed` / `-no-major` / `-overwrite` / `-claims` | all exit 0 |

Tests were run from the repo root, never `pnpm --filter pkg exec vitest` (objectui#3378). The pin file is **in** the type-check program — `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit --listFiles` lists `ViewSwitcher.tsx`, `ObjectView.tsx`, `ViewSwitcher.test.tsx` and the new pin, so the `@ts-expect-error` legs are live and not erased by an `exclude`.

### Published surface: byte-identical, measured

`packages/plugin-view` was built from these sources and from the base, and all **13** emitted files compare equal by sha256 — `VERDICT: dist/ is BYTE-IDENTICAL across the repair`. `satisfies` and a totality assert are erased before emit and none of the four tables is exported. The source swap was proven on disk before each build and the restore by an empty `git diff HEAD -- packages/plugin-view/src`. That is why the changeset declares an **empty frontmatter** (the exemption `check-changeset-presence.mjs` names explicitly, and which it confirmed in its own verdict line) rather than a `patch`, and why no consumer package owes a test here.

### Ablations — predicted, then run

Each ran through `ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor must hit a declared number of times, the write is verified against the disk (anchor count, blob hash, control bytes), and the restore is proven by blob-hash equality with `HEAD` **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`, under a trap on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths. No dist preflight: every subject is read by `tsc` or `vitest` from source in the package under test, not through a dependency's `dist/`.

**A1 — delete the totality assert for `DEFAULT_VIEW_LABELS` (the ablation the dispatch names).**
Predicted: the added-member pin goes red and the compiler says nothing.
Observed, exactly that: `TYPECHECK_EXIT=0` — **the compiler is silent** — and the pin file reports `1 failed | 14 passed`, the failure being ``ViewSwitcher.tsx / DEFAULT_VIEW_LABELS keeps the added-member assert beside it``. ⇒ the pin is the *only* instrument that catches a dropped guard, which is the whole reason it exists.

**A2 — delete a real row (`chart: 'Chart',`) from `DEFAULT_VIEW_LABELS`.**
Predicted: TS2344 at the assert, on the real table against the real `ViewType`.
Observed: `TYPECHECK_EXIT=2`, `src/ViewSwitcher.tsx(109,41): error TS2344: Type '"chart"' does not satisfy the constraint 'never'.` — plus a TS7053 at the index site, the same fact from the consumer's side. ⇒ objectui#5321 / objectui#8127's added-member guard survived the repair, measured on the real union and not only in simulation.

**A3 — disable the gate's `satisfies` unwrap.**
Predicted: the icon gate errors with a short read on both plugin-view anchors.
Observed: `GATE_EXIT=1` with ``yielded 0 entries, fewer than the 9`` on **both** `iconMap` and `DEFAULT_VIEW_ICONS`, and the gate's own suite `4 failed | 47 passed` — including the two new wrapper cases, so they are not vacuous.

**A4 — revert `parseMapEntries` to the `};` search. ⚠️ PREDICTION FALSIFIED.**
Predicted red. Observed **green**: `Test Files 1 passed`, `SUITE_EXIT=0`. Measured directly afterwards: the old reader over-reads **392 characters** past the literal (the totality assert plus the head of the sibling `return` object), and none of those lines matches the `key: value,` shape the entry regex wants, so the parse is unchanged — 12 identical keys under both readers. The hazard is therefore **latent, not live**: one `label: something,` added to that block would make it a 13th entry. The hardening stays and the comment beside it was rewritten to state the measurement instead of the prediction (commit `ec37341d9`).

## Why this card is dispatchable while the priority gate is closed

`docs/NORTH-STAR.md` (charter, landed 2026-09-18T23:33:58Z) clause 3 bans dispatching p2/p3 tool and contract-hygiene cards while the product repos hold open P0/P1 — and they do (objectui 0/7, objectstack 4/52, read 2026-09-18T23:42Z). This card is taken under the clause's **second half**, quoted 照抄不译:

> 产品仓还有开放的 P0/P1 时,任何车道不派 p2/p3 的工具卡、契约卫生卡;**解锁产品 P0/P1 的仪器卡沿链继承其优先级。**

objectui#9860 is `priority:p1`, `pm:blocked`, `Blocked-by: #9943`; this card is the remaining break holding PR objectui#9877, the spec-`main` shape gate. ⇒ finishing it unblocks a P1. The `priority:p2` label stays exactly as triage set it — inheritance is a **selection** fact, not a re-grade.

## What was NOT run, and why

- **The spec-`main` leg.** The card's red reading came through objectui#9860's injection mechanism, which lives in **PR objectui#9877 — HELD and unmerged**. ⛔ Not run, and its absence is not reported as a failure. The type-level property is measured directly instead: the pins are the instrument, and both legs are takeable on the installed spec today.
- **The cascade.** The 5 × TS7016 + 1 × TS7006 that `app-shell` and `example-byo-backend-console` report on that leg are cascade of these three rows — not independent defects, and not chased here.

## Delivery

Draft, and it stops here — no ready flip, no auto-merge, no CI wait; the dispatching seat lands it. This repo's `AGENTS.md` tells a green non-governed PR author to self-merge; that clause and this dispatch conflict, the conflict is filed as objectstack-ai/objectstack#19128, and until it is ruled this PR sits on the stricter side. No dev-applied label (this repo names none and forbids `skip-changeset`).
